`statci` brings software-engineering-grade continuous integration to statistical R pipelines and Quarto/RMarkdown manuscripts. This vignette walks through:

1. Auditing R scripts and Quarto documents with the AST-based statistical linter.
2. Suppressing intentional exceptions and registering custom AST rules.
3. Cross-checking numerical claims in manuscripts against fitted R model objects.
4. Combining results into standalone HTML/Markdown audit reports and generating a GitHub Actions workflow.

```{r setup}
library(statci)
```

## 1. Inspecting Built-In Statistical Lint Rules

`statci` ships 14 built-in AST rules targeting reproducibility, parallel RNG safety, duplicate worker seeds, train/test data leakage, multilevel centering, missingness/factor hazards, floating-point comparisons, and multiple-testing inflation:

```{r list-rules}
list_stat_rules()[, c("id", "severity", "category", "title")]
```

## 2. Linting R Scripts and Quarto Documents

Unlike style linters, `stat_lint()` parses full R syntax trees via `xmlparsedata` and `xml2`. Let's inspect a small analysis script with several silent methodological flaws:

```{r lint-script}
flawed_script <- '
df <- read.csv("/Users/researcher/Desktop/study.csv")
df$x <- scale(df$x)
idx <- sample(nrow(df), 80)
train <- df[idx, ]

fit <- lme4::lmer(y ~ x * w + (1 + x | school), data = train)
pvals <- sapply(1:10, function(j) t.test(rnorm(20), rnorm(20), var.equal = F)$p.value)
'

lint_bad <- stat_lint_text(flawed_script)
lint_bad
```

Notice how `statci` pinpoints each distinct statistical hazard—hardcoded personal paths, unseeded stochasticity, preprocessing before data splitting, uncentered multilevel interactions, missing convergence/singularity checks, unadjusted multiple testing, and mutable `F` instead of `FALSE`—with exact line and column coordinates.

### Exact Line Mapping and Cross-Chunk Scope in Quarto (`.qmd`)

For `.qmd` and `.Rmd` files, `statci` projects all R chunks into a blank-line-preserving AST so line numbers match the original document exactly and state flows cleanly across chunks:

```{r lint-qmd}
fence <- paste(rep("`", 3), collapse = "")
qmd_doc <- paste(
  "---",
  'title: "Treatment Analysis"',
  "---",
  "",
  "We begin by setting a global seed in our setup chunk.",
  "",
  paste0(fence, "{r qmd-setup}"),
  "set.seed(2026)",
  fence,
  "",
  "Next we simulate and run a clean regression, with one intentional float comparison:",
  "",
  paste0(fence, "{r}"),
  "#| label: check-mean",
  "x <- rnorm(100)",
  "flag <- mean(x) == 0.0",
  fence,
  sep = "\n"
)

qmd_lint <- stat_lint_text(qmd_doc, format = "qmd")
qmd_lint
```

Notice that `rnorm(100)` on line 15 is recognized as seeded by `set.seed(2026)` in the earlier `qmd-setup` chunk, while `mean(x) == 0.0` is flagged at exact line 16 in chunk `check-mean`.

### Inline Suppressions and Custom Rules

Intentional exceptions can be silenced with `# statci-ignore` or `# statci-ignore: <rule_id>`, and teams can register project-specific AST rules with `new_stat_rule()` and `register_stat_rule()`:

```{r custom-rule}
no_attach_rule <- new_stat_rule(
  id = "no_attach_call",
  title = "Avoid attach() in reproducible analyses",
  severity = "warning",
  category = "hygiene",
  description = "attach() alters the search path and risks silent variable masking.",
  recommendation = "Use explicit data$col references or with().",
  check = function(ctx) {
    out <- list()
    for (u in ctx$units) {
      nds <- xml2::xml_find_all(u$xml, ".//SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL[text() = 'attach']")
      for (nd in nds) {
        out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- list(
          line = as.integer(xml2::xml_attr(nd, "line1")) + u$line_offset,
          col = as.integer(xml2::xml_attr(nd, "col1")),
          message = "Avoid attach(); pass `data =` explicitly to modeling functions."
        )
      }
    }
    out
  }
)

stat_lint_text("attach(mtcars)\n", rules = list(no_attach_rule))
```

## 3. Manuscript-to-Code Consistency Auditing

Copy-pasted numbers in manuscripts frequently drift out of sync when datasets are cleaned or covariates change. `audit_manuscript()` and `audit_manuscript_text()` cross-check prose statistics against actual fitted R model objects (`lm`, `glm`, `lmerMod`, `htest`, or tidy data frames) using rounding-aware tolerance rules.

```{r manuscript-audit}
set.seed(42)
study_df <- data.frame(
  treatment = rbinom(150, 1, 0.5),
  baseline = rnorm(150)
)
study_df$outcome <- 2.0 + 0.65 * study_df$treatment - 0.30 * study_df$baseline +
  rnorm(150, sd = 0.8)

fit_primary <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + baseline, data = study_df)
sm <- summary(fit_primary)$coefficients
ci <- confint(fit_primary)

# Suppose an author accidentally copied a flipped sign for baseline and a stale N = 160
draft_qmd <- paste(
  "---",
  "title: Main Results",
  "---",
  "",
  "<!-- statci: model=primary term=treatment -->",
  sprintf(
    "Treatment significantly improved outcomes (*b* = %.2f, SE = %.2f, 95%% CI [%.2f, %.2f], *p* < .001).",
    sm["treatment", 1], sm["treatment", 2], ci["treatment", 1], ci["treatment", 2]
  ),
  "",
  "<!-- statci: model=primary term=baseline -->",
  sprintf(
    "Baseline score was positively associated with outcome (*b* = %.2f), across *N* = 160 participants.",
    abs(sm["baseline", 1]) # Oops! Sign flipped from negative to positive, and N is stale
  ),
  sep = "\n"
)

ms_audit <- audit_manuscript_text(draft_qmd, models = list(primary = fit_primary))
ms_audit
```

Every verified claim—including passing rounded matches, sign flips, and stale sample sizes—is returned in `as_tibble(ms_audit)`:

```{r ms-tibble}
as_tibble(ms_audit)[, c("line", "term", "metric", "reported_raw", "actual", "issue_type", "status")]
```

## 4. Unified Reports, CI Gates & GitHub Actions

Combine verification results into a unified `statci_report()`, render standalone HTML or GitHub-Flavored Markdown summaries, and enforce automated pass/warn/fail gates:

```{r report-and-gha}
clean_lint <- stat_lint_text("set.seed(2026)\nx <- rnorm(50)\n")
rep <- statci_report(
  lint = clean_lint,
  manuscript = ms_audit,
  title = "Study Replication Audit"
)
rep

# Render Markdown summary suitable for $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
md_summary <- render_statci_report(rep, format = "markdown")
cat(substr(md_summary, 1, 600), "...\n")

# Generate a ready-to-use GitHub Actions workflow in a temporary project directory
tmp_proj <- tempfile("statci_demo_")
dir.create(tmp_proj)
wf_path <- use_statci_github_action(
  path = tmp_proj,
  lint_paths = c("R", "analysis"),
  manuscript = "manuscript.qmd",
  models_path = "models/fits.rds"
)
cat(head(readLines(wf_path), 24), sep = "\n")
unlink(tmp_proj, recursive = TRUE)
```
